# World Monitor Public Interfaces

> Machine-readable entry point for the public-only fork: anonymous documentation MCP, in-browser WebMCP, supported public REST request shapes, and static reference data.

These are distinct interfaces, not interchangeable transports sharing a product tool inventory. This fork has no accounts, subscriptions, account keys, or paid plans. Preferences are local; anonymous access still has endpoint-specific limits.

This is the API-section companion to the [site-wide briefing](https://www.worldmonitor.app/llms.txt) and [human documentation](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/llms.txt). Retained upstream methodology and client references are not promises that all upstream operations ship in this fork.

## Interfaces

- [Documentation MCP](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/mcp): anonymous documentation search and retrieval over Streamable HTTP. The `api/docs-mcp.ts` facade proxies the upstream Mintlify transport; it does not define a local documentation tool inventory or serve live product data. Use `tools/list` for upstream protocol discovery; see the [docs server card](https://www.worldmonitor.app/.well-known/mcp/docs-server-card.json). A plain GET to the transport can return 405.
- **Browser WebMCP:** in-page dashboard tools registered through the browser's `modelContext` provider where supported, not an HTTP product MCP endpoint. `get_dashboard_context`, `list_map_layers`, and `get_access_context` expose bounded visible state and public dashboard capabilities.
- [Public REST base](https://api.worldmonitor.app): use supported public request shapes with a descriptive User-Agent; for example `/api/news/v1/list-feed-digest?variant=full&lang=en&public=1`. Public availability is route- and request-shape-specific, not a blanket entitlement to every operation in the upstream specification.
- [OpenAPI YAML](https://www.worldmonitor.app/openapi.yaml) and [OpenAPI JSON](https://www.worldmonitor.app/openapi.json): retained REST schema references. Confirm fork route availability before calling an upstream operation.
- [Sandbox index](https://www.worldmonitor.app/sandbox/index.json): deterministic static samples of upstream REST responses, not live data or an API entitlement.
- [Agent Skills discovery manifest](https://worldmonitor.app/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json): retained upstream recipes; check supported fork interfaces before executing them.
- [Agent Plugin metadata](https://www.worldmonitor.app/plugin.json): public metadata for the Agent Plugins 1.0.0 repository package.

## Common Tasks

- **Dashboard context and discovery:** use browser WebMCP `get_dashboard_context`, `list_map_layers`, and `list_dashboard_panels` to inspect what the current dashboard exposes.
- [Country reference pages](https://www.worldmonitor.app/countries/): source-attributed country corpus and published snapshots. Browser WebMCP `openCountryBrief` opens the dashboard country context.
- [Country situation brief sample](https://www.worldmonitor.app/sandbox/get-country-intel-brief.json): static example for parser development; it does not advertise a live country-brief API.
- [Country risk and resilience sample](https://www.worldmonitor.app/sandbox/get-resilience-score.json): static example of upstream score, domain breakdown, trend, and confidence.
- [Chokepoint references](https://www.worldmonitor.app/chokepoints/): correlate physical supply signals with market context. Check source coverage and observation times before inferring a transmission path.
- **Live situational awareness:** inspect news, aviation, natural-disaster and infrastructure layers in the public dashboard; visible observations remain subject to source availability and coverage limitations.
- **Forecast context:** distinguish published forecast context and prediction-market prices from observed events. This fork does not advertise a forecast-generation service.

## Snapshot and Corpus Provenance

The country corpus retains published country snapshots, capture dates, methodology, source attribution and licensing limits. A committed snapshot is evidence captured at its stated time, not a fresh runtime query. The extended corpus preserves upstream methodology and references without restoring retired product MCP tools or account-backed APIs.

- [Extended LLM corpus](https://www.worldmonitor.app/llms-full.txt): generated reference material, country ranking snapshots, methodology, and provenance.
- [Source catalog](https://www.worldmonitor.app/sources/): provider identity, source coverage and attribution.
- [AI search briefing](https://www.worldmonitor.app/ai-search.md): generated coverage figures with a reconciliation date.

## Retained Upstream Client References

The upstream CLI, SDKs and documentation remain useful schema and methodology references. Their full operation inventory is not supported merely because the sources remain in this repository.

- [Upstream CLI](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/cli): check public fork routes rather than assuming upstream product MCP calls work here.
- [Upstream SDK guide](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/sdks): Python, Ruby, Go, and JavaScript client references; check fork operation availability.
- [Developer portal](https://www.worldmonitor.app/developers.md): retained upstream integration reference.
- [REST versioning reference](https://www.worldmonitor.app/api-versioning.md): upstream compatibility and deprecation methodology, not a new fork service-level commitment.

- [Human API docs](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/documentation): retained upstream documentation.
